LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING LISTENING COMPREHENSION

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.1: Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension, part of Strand 1 in Grade 5 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why should we say the sounds in words, phrases, and sentences correctly? 2. How can we improve our pronunciation? 3. Why should we listen attentively?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. listen to an oral narrative in pairs or groups,

2. identify words and phrases containing the sounds /ʌ/ /ɑː / from a print or audio text,

3. say words and phrases related to the theme accurately,

4. construct sentences using words and phrases with peers. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. listen to an oral narrative in pairs or groups,
2. identify words and phrases containing the sounds /ʌ/ /ɑː / from a print or audio text,
3. say words and phrases related to the theme accurately,
4. construct sentences using words and phrases with peers. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking Listening Comprehension together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration is developed as the learner works with peers to construct sentences.

• Digital Literacy is enhanced when the learner uses electronic devices to listen and record themselves.

• Learning to Learn is instilled as the learner adopts the use of correct pronunciation in various contexts for effective

communication.

Values:
Responsibility is inculcated as the learner learns about child rights and responsibilities, and practises them while

making an audio recording of a poem containing the target sounds and playing the audio for effective feedback.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Life Skills: Effective communication is achieved as the learner articulates the target sounds clearly and also listen to

audio of the target sound.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can link the content of child rights when they learn about child rights and responsibilities in Social Studies.
